assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made a superconducting artificial atom strongly coupled to a single microwave photon in an on-chip resonator, giving dispersive readout, two-qubit coupling and the transmon-era architecture used in essentially every superconducting processor. It opened a genuinely new regime of light-matter interaction (strong and ultrastrong coupling in solid state) and underpins a large body of experiments reproduced across many laboratories. Clear, original and lasting; a natural complement to the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits.
assessment.attribution: Blais and Schoelkopf with Wallraff and colleagues proposed (2004) and demonstrated strong coupling, so Blais (theory) plus Schoelkopf and Wallraff (experiment) is a coherent trio. Yale-group contributors beyond these names and the relation to the 2025 laureates' work are potential credit questions, but the supplied three are a defensible core.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of independent confirmation, stable interpretation, and wide adoption; the discovery stands apart from the still-unfinished goal of fault-tolerant computing, so recognition is timely and not hype-driven.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize's circuit lineage may make the committee reluctant to reward superconducting circuits again so soon.
I work in this field and may have conflicts of interest, so my judgment should be discounted accordingly.
Division of credit between the 2004 proposal and the first experiments, and the role of the transmon, is not resolved by the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller's 1995 proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions, and its experimental realisation with high-fidelity gates, entanglement and small algorithms, established the first scalable-in-principle quantum computing platform and set the template for controlled many-body quantum engineering. The physics is fundamental and the impact on quantum information is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller as theory originators and Blatt as leading experimental realiser form a good configuration. Wineland already received the 2012 prize for trapped-ion control, and the Innsbruck experimental credit may need to be weighed against NIST contributions not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: The scheme was validated by many independent groups over 25+ years; platform performance is mature, though practical large-scale computing is still ahead.
uncertainties: Overlap with Wineland's 2012 recognition and with the broader atomic quantum-information candidate B008.
Whether the prize should honour the computing proposal or the experimental demonstrations is unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on magic-wavelength trapping, reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and opened tests of relativity, searches for varying constants, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second. It is an experiment that makes a basic quantum phenomenon visible and controllable with extreme attention to physical detail.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye drove the performance frontier, so a two-person prize is natural. Contributions from Hall/Hänsch combs (already rewarded in 2005) and other lattice clock groups are separate, and the supplied credit is clean.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs reproduce and compare clocks at the 1e-18 level; the redefinition of the second is still pending but the science is mature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers recognition after the redefinition of the second.
Fractional credit relative to ion clock work (Wineland, Rosenband) is not addressed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cooling macroscopic mechanical oscillators to their quantum ground state and entangling or coherently controlling them with photons or superconducting qubits shows quantum mechanics at massive scale and links to the macroscopic-quantum theme. Original and conceptually clean, with relevance to sensing and transduction. I know related work on phonons coupled to artificial atoms first hand.
assessment.attribution: Five credited names exceed the three-laureate limit, so choose Cleland (first quantum-ground-state mechanical resonator and qubit-phonon control), Teufel (sideband cooling in microwave circuits), and Aspelmeyer (optomechanical entanglement and quantum optomechanics). Kippenberg and Painter are equally strong, so the selection is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Core results are reproduced across microwave, optical and phononic platforms; applications are still maturing, so it is moderately mature, perhaps slightly early.
uncertainties: Selecting three of five equally plausible contributors is arbitrary and may leave out Painter and Kippenberg.
Distinct sub-discoveries (ground-state cooling, entanglement, qubit control) may need different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators, the quantum spin Hall effect and the quantum anomalous Hall effect established a new classification of electronic phases with protected edge states, a major conceptual advance with experimental confirmation. I defer to colleagues on materials details.
assessment.attribution: Kane (theory), Molenkamp (HgTe quantum spin Hall experiment) and Xue (quantum anomalous Hall) cover distinct decisive steps, but Mele, Bernevig, Zhang and Hasan have strong claims, so allocation is a serious unresolved issue. The related candidate B045 lists a different group.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with a vast literature, though applications remain limited.
uncertainties: Credit disputes around Zhang, Bernevig, Mele and Hasan are not resolved here.
Compound candidate: QSH and QAH may deserve different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including the superfluid-Mott transition, single-site imaging and engineered Hamiltonians, made strongly correlated many-body physics controllable and observable. It created a new regime of experimental condensed-matter-like physics with broad independent confirmation.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Cirac (with Jaksch) provided the theoretical proposals and Bloch (with Greiner) the decisive experiments; Greiner's role in the Mott transition and microscopy is also strong, so the three-person limit forces a difficult choice. Overlap in names with the trapped-ion candidate may stretch the same theorists.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed across many labs for 20+ years; quantum advantage in simulation is still developing.
uncertainties: Reusing Cirac and Zoller across candidates raises a fairness issue for prize configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction showed that fragile quantum information can be protected, creating the theoretical foundation for fault-tolerant computation. Its conceptual importance is great, and experimental demonstrations of below-threshold logical qubits are now emerging.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane share the first codes and Kitaev the topological codes and fault tolerance; Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme and others also have strong claims, so allocation is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: The theory is mature, but experimental realisation of useful fault-tolerant machines is still ahead. I am wary of rewarding application promise early, so I rank it lower.
uncertainties: Experimental validation is recent and limited to small codes.
Many plausible contributors outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene revealed correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable moire flat band, opening the whole field of moire quantum materials. It is a new regime of physics with strong reproducibility across laboratories. Outside my main area, so I defer to colleagues on materials details.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat band at the magic angle, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experiments; Cao and Fatemi, as junior experimental authors, are outside the supplied credit and Kim and Dean's related work may also merit consideration.
assessment.maturity: Discovered in 2018 and confirmed independently, but the nature of the superconductivity is still debated, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Interpretation of the superconducting and correlated states remains unsettled.
Relation to other moire platforms such as transition-metal dichalcogenides is not resolved.
